candidate_reports.remark: Flooded washes and low water crossings near Sanostee_ making roads impassable_ including BIA Road 5012.
New Mexico State Highway 170 washed out at mile marker 3.
New Mexico State Highway 170 washed out at mile marker 18.
Tico Time RV Park became flooded from the nearby Animas River with standing water several inches deep inundating the park grounds.
River flooding along U.S. Highway 550 between Aztec and New Mexico-Colorado border. River is flooding the highway.
Low water crossing impassable on Arizona Rd.
Low lying areas near the San Juan River are flooding and people are leaving the area.
Tree limbs and power lines blown down in straight-line winds with power outages in Gallup between south 2nd street_ Burke_ Aztec_ and Country Club Dr.
Knights of Columbus building in Gallup sustained roof damage from straight-line wind gusts. Roofing material was blown off of the building.
Low water crossing impassable on County Road 3000.
NM Road 112 closed just south of El Vado due to flooding.
Low water crossing impassable.
Highway 173 impassable due to water flowing over road.
NM Road 124 was closed at mile marker 19 (Casa Blanca/Paraje) due to flooding.
Fast-flowing water over Highway 550.
Highway 173 impassable due to mud and water flowing over road.
NM Highway 511 and US 64 are impassable due to flowing water and mud over the roads.
Indian Service Road 36 washed out and impassable due to flows through an arroyo.
Road 4599 impassable due to mud and water flowing across road.
Highway 173 collapsed_ making the road impassable.
Highway 64 at junction with Highway 511 closed due to mud and debris across road.
An extended stretch of US Highway 64 is closed from Navajo City to 11 miles west of Dulce due to flooding.
Homes near Gobernador Canyon evacuated due to flooding.
Corrects previous report from Abiquiu. Video on X showed the Rio Chama out of its banks_ impacting homes along the River just south of US Highway 84 in Chama.
Video on X shows the Rio Chama out of its banks with flooding just south of Highway 64 near an RV park.
Report of homes being evacuated in Chama due to rising water along a tributary that feeds into the Rio Chama. Location estimated.
Highway 17 closed from Chama to the Colorado border due to flooding along the Rio Chama.
US Highway 64 closed in both directions due to flooding on the Rio Chama.
Evacuations of low-lying properties along the Animas River on Road 2900.
Water in La Plata River reaching bottom of bridge on Pinon Hills Road and still rising.
Water flooding over Calle de Rio from San Juan River.
Water from San Juan River 2 feet deep over Road 5005.
Evacuations from homes on Road 3020 (3021 on some maps).
Water running over the north approach to bridge over San Juan River on Road 5500. Closing bridge until further notice.
Resident evacuated near Highway 170 near CO State line from floodwaters in the La Plata River.
Wild Horse neighborhood had access closed down from Highway 64 due to flood waters in San Juan River.
Animas River flooding on County Road 2916 and up to edge of Highway 550.
Animas river breached a brick wall at Boyd Park_ allowing floodwaters to enter the park.
Fire crews evacuating residences along County Road 2380 due to flooding along Animas River.
La Plata River has begun to inundate houses at the junction of Highway 574 and 170. Evacuations ongoing.
Willow Creek has exceeded its banks and was flooding. The water was up to the Rutheron Bridge road surface along NM State Highway 95_ but the road was still passable.
Smokey Bear RAWS.

Images on social media show massive amounts of earth washed out at the Cumbres & Toltec Railroad bridge where train tracks across the Rio Chama. The damage to the railroad bridge has rendered it unusable.
Swift water rescue for a couple in the La Plata River floodwaters.
South Miller Avenue Bridge over Animas River is closed due to water over road.
Santa Fe SNOTEL.
Palo SNOTEL.
North Costilla SNOTEL.
Taos Pueblo SNOTEL.
Bateman SNOTEL.
Vacas Locas SNOTEL.
Hopewell SNOTEL.
Taos Powderhorn SNOTEL.
NM Highway 95 closed at mile marker 13 due to flooding.
Pinon Hills Blvd bridge over Animas River overtopped. Debris on upstream side pushing running water over bridge.
Swift water rescue of 1 individual off Murray Bridge over Animas River.
